<reason>CON won a close, high-clash debate by narrowing the live zone after PRO’s concessions: heavy offloading fails (or is lied about) under both rules, light use is unrestricted under both, and logs plus oral defense do not uniquely verify process. That left default permission changing mainly the middle student who outsources thinking with a receipt. CON’s writing-as-the-skill / calculator weighing and the self-incrimination turn made that comparison easier to vote on than PRO’s otherwise sharp “failing receipt vs. A with no receipt” frame. PRO never showed how the default, rather than targeted unaided hours, creates the struggle for the marginal pre-college writer.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON’s R2 turn that PRO’s incomplete/rewrite for a truthful “thesis/outline/draft by model” log makes heavy disclosure self-incriminating, collapsing the honesty advantage transparency was supposed to buy.</best_rebuttal>
